mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (exceeding 25 basis points in a single month) signals an imminent monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 10%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions and rising consumer spending, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE>10%), a decline in UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the decline signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (exceeding 1% in a single month) indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 1 month fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the decline signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of retail sales (RSAFS above 400,000 million dollars) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS above 400,000 million dollars fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (exceeding 3.0% annualized) signals rising inflation, which may prompt the Fed to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 3.0% fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a strong labor market without monetary tightening, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining UNRATE and stable FEDFUNDS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.
